title: Administrator
description:
Job Title: Administrator

Location: Worcester, UK - Hybrid

Salary: 11,200 actual salary based on a full-time equivalent of 28,000 (0.4 FTE, 2 days per week)

Job Type: Permanent, Part-time remote home-working, within a commutable distance of the Worcester office. Home/office split to be agreed.

Are you an organised, proactive administrator looking for a rewarding role where you can make a real difference?

Music Therapy Works is looking for an Administrator to play a central role in supporting the operational efficiency of our charity. This varied role provides administrative, financial, HR and governance support, working closely with the CEO, Clinical Lead, music therapists, trustees, contractors and external stakeholders to ensure the organisation runs smoothly, securely and professionally.

Key Responsibilities:

Clients:
- Maintain secure, accurate and up-to-date client records from initial enquiry or referral onwards.
- Coordinate client documentation, including contracts, consent forms, risk assessments, letters of assurance, forecast hours and evaluation surveys.
- Support the CEO and Clinical Lead in coordinating music therapist caseloads.
- Manage routine correspondence with existing and prospective clients, ensuring confidentiality and data protection.

Our People:
- Coordinate recruitment and onboarding of employees, contractors and trustees.
- Maintain secure records for trustees, employees, contractors, volunteers and placement students.
- Administer routine HR processes, including annual leave, absence tracking and draft contracts.
- Coordinate DBS checks and provide professional administrative support to the wider team.

Finance & Governance:
- Support the Finance Officer with information for client invoicing and staff payroll.
- Maintain records for funders and donors and undertake routine financial administration, including paying in cheques.
- Take and distribute accurate minutes for Board and subcommittee meetings.
- Coordinate the filing, review and distribution of organisational policies and support effective governance administration.

General Administration:
- Maintain organised, accurate and secure physical and digital filing systems.
- Coordinate room bookings, online meetings, away days, training days and other events.
- Maintain the company asset register.
- Administer digital workspaces and tools, including Microsoft 365 and Apple Business.
- Identify opportunities to improve administrative processes and efficiency.
- Undertake other duties commensurate with the role as required.

What can we offer you in return?

You'll be joining Music Therapy Works at an exciting time, with the opportunity to play an important role in supporting the organisation's continued development and impact.

We offer a flexible hybrid working arrangement, with part-time home-working and time spent at our Worcester office as agreed.

You'll also benefit from:
- 33 days' holiday per year (FTE).
- NEST pension.
- Cyclescheme.
- Safeguarding training.
- Enhanced DBS check.
- A supportive and purpose-driven working environment.
- The opportunity to develop your skills and contribute to the work of a specialist organisation making a positive difference through music therapy.

About You:

If you join the team, we'll provide you with the support and training you need to succeed in the role and develop your skills.

To succeed in this role, you will bring the following skills, experience and behaviours:
- Proven experience in an administrative or office management role.
- Excellent IT skills, including Microsoft 365 applications such as Outlook, Excel, Word, Teams, OneDrive and SharePoint.
- Experience of accurately taking and producing minutes for professional meetings.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt your communication appropriately when working with employees, trustees, contractors, customers, partner organisations, funders and donors.
- Experience of organising and maintaining confidential filing systems and sensitive records.
- Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to coordinate bookings, meetings, events and competing priorities effectively.
- Experience of supporting basic HR processes, such as annual leave and absence tracking.
- Confidence in supporting financial administration, including payroll and invoicing processes.
- A strong understanding of confidentiality, data protection and the importance of securely managing sensitive information.
- A proactive, reliable and highly organised approach to work.
- The ability to work independently while also contributing positively as part of a wider team.
- Willingness to use AI tools and develop AI-related skills to improve efficiency and ways of working.
- Ability to work flexibly between home and the Worcester office.

Desirable experience includes:
- Experience of working or volunteering within a charity or third-sector organisation.
- Familiarity with a clinical, medical or therapeutic setting.
- Experience maintaining records for funders and donors.
- Basic knowledge of, or confidence in, preparing draft contracts using templates.
- Experience administering CRM systems.
- Knowledge and experience of using Apple Business.

Important dates for consideration:
- 20thSeptember: deadline for applications.
- 25thSeptember: invitations to first interview.
- 6th& 7th October: first interviews, online.
- 8thOctober: invitations to second interview.
- 13thOctober: second interviews, in person only at The Hive, Worcester, WR1 3 PD.

Employees are required to complete an Enhanced DBS check for the Child and Adult Workforce.

Interested candidates are invited to submit their CV.

title: Production Administrator
description:
Production Administrator

Location: Worcestershire, DY10 4 JB
Salary: £30,000 and £35,000, depending on experience
Contract: Full Time Permanent

What We Offer
- A stable position within a busy and well-established UK manufacturing business.
- A supportive working environment with real responsibility and involvement in day-to-day production.
- The opportunity to develop experience across production planning, manufacturing operations and ERP systems.
- Training and support to develop your understanding of our products, manufacturing processes and systems.
- The opportunity to become an integral part of the team responsible for keeping production organised, controlled and moving to programme.

Benweld Secure Manufacturing / Fabrication

Benweld Secure is looking for an organised and proactive Production Administrator to support the day-to-day operation of our busy manufacturing department.

Working closely with the Production Planning Manager, you will play an important role in ensuring production information, works orders, job progress and ERP records are accurate, controlled and kept up to date.

This is a predominantly office-based role but requires regular communication with our production teams. It would suit someone who is comfortable working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment where priorities can change and accurate information is essential to keeping production moving.

Key Responsibilities
- Issue, maintain and control works orders, job packs and production documentation.
- Update ERP/MRP systems with job progress, labour hours, material movements and completed operations.
- Track jobs through each stage of production, including fabrication, welding, finishing, subcontract processes and despatch.
- Support the Production Planning Manager with daily production priorities, workload planning and short-term schedule changes.
- Liaise directly with supervisors and shopfloor teams to obtain progress updates and ensure production plans accurately reflect the current position.
- Monitor outstanding operations and highlight potential delays, shortages or production issues.
- Maintain accurate production paperwork, records and material/product traceability.
- Assist with closing completed works orders and ensuring all required information has been correctly recorded.
- Liaise with Production, Planning, Stores, Purchasing, Quality and Despatch to help maintain the smooth flow of work through the factory.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date information within ERP/MRP systems such as EFACS, supporting production planning, reporting and traceability.
- Assist with general production administration and reporting as required.

What We're Looking For
- Previous experience in an administration or production support role, ideally within a manufacturing or engineering environment.
- Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Confident using Microsoft Excel and computer-based business systems.
- Comfortable working with data and maintaining accurate records.
- Able to communicate confidently with shopfloor teams, supervisors and managers.
- Proactive and willing to chase information when required rather than waiting for updates.
- Able to manage changing priorities and work effectively in a busy production environment.
- Reliable, methodical and able to take ownership of allocated tasks.

Desirable Experience

Experience in the following would be beneficial, although training can be provided:
- Fabrication, welding or engineered manufacturing environments.
- ERP/MRP systems, particularly EFACS or similar manufacturing software.
- Works orders, job cards, route cards and production documentation.
- Production planning, scheduling or capacity planning.
- Manufacturing traceability and quality-controlled documentation.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong administrative skills who wants to develop their career within production planning and manufacturing operations.

If you feel you have the necessary skills and experience to be successful in this role, click on APPLY today, forwarding an up-to-date copy of your CV for consideration in the first instance.

No Agencies Please

title: Ward Clerk Maternity
description: If you are ready for a challenge and want to be part of a team providing an excellent administration and reception service, then this might be just what you are looking for. We are looking to recruit enthusiastic and motivated people who are organised , flexible and adaptable to join our team of ward clerks. You will need to have excellent organisational, communication and IT skills, job specific training will be given. This is a pivotal role which requires someone who is able to work independently and is self-motivated. You will be able to deliver a high standard of customer service and communicate effectively. The role is full time covering a shift pattern that is worked over 4 days including working 2 nights per week. Job Purpose: To provide administrative and clerical support to the clinical and midwifery staff within maternity services. To ensure the availability of accurate patient records and documentation as per Trust policies and procedures. To liaise with patients, relatives and other members of the public politely and efficiently, ensuring confidentiality and security of patient information as per Trust policy and in line with Information Governance guidance Key Duties: To provide a reception service, handling initial enquiries, gathering basic information and taking initial action within defined protocols to assist in resolving any queries To keep staff informed of admissions and discharges, and to ensure queries from other members of staff and members of the public are dealt with appropriately either in person or on the telephone. To receive general telephone calls, recording messages and responding to initial enquiries, referring the call to the relevant member of staff, as appropriate. To make telephone calls on behalf of the Midwives as directed. To assist in admitting and discharging patients using manual and computerised systems. To file reports, correspondence, forms, etc. in patients notes in an ordered manner, to facilitate the efficient retrieval of such documentation on request. To update and maintain filing systems in the ward/department to enable timely and accurate information retrieval. To arrange transport between departments and to destinations outside the hospital, as required. To assist with housekeeping duties within ward/department. To maintain effective communication with ward clerk / clerical team assistant colleagues within the department. To provide relief cover within the Directorate undertaking any duties within the scope of the ward clerk / clerical team assistant role. Arrange follow up appointments for patients prior to discharge

title: Senior Medical Receptionist Care Navigator
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced and motivated primary care professional to join our friendly and supportive practice. This varied role combines patient-facing reception and care navigation with scanning, coding and administrative duties. You will be one of the 1st points of contact for our patients, providing a professional, welcoming and helpful service; ensuring patients are directed to the most appropriate service or healthcare professional. We are looking for someone who has the skills and enthusiasm to take on a senior role within our existing team, with the potential to progress into a formal Team Leader position. The successful candidate will work within the reception and care navigation team. They will have a forward-thinking approach, be confident taking responsibility and able to provide guidance and support to colleagues when needed, working closely with the management team. The role will include: Reception, appointment booking and care navigation Scanning, coding and processing clinical correspondence Administrative duties Supporting colleagues Organising and prioritising team workloads Identifying opportunities to improve processes and patient experience Working closely with the management team Previous primary care experience, excellent communication skills, strong IT skills and the ability to prioritise and multitask in a busy environment are essential. Reception Duties Provide an effective and efficient reception service to patients and visitors at the practice. Open the premises at the start of the day, ensuring all necessary checks and preparations are completed to receive patients. Secure the building at the end of the day, ensuring all areas are fully secured. Handle general enquiries and process appointment requests from patients via phone, online, or in person, updating the EMIS clinical system accordingly. Process repeat prescription requests. Receive and distribute both internal and external mail and documentation. Ensure accurate and timely logging of messages for clinicians regarding emergency appointment requests and home visits. Coordinate with third-party agencies to arrange patient care as directed by GP's. Maintain and accurately enter data into the practices computer system and patients' electronic records, which may include scanning and coding clinical information in line with practice protocols. Reception and Administrative Duties: Leadership: Ensure the delivery of high-quality patient services within a safe and efficient work environment by providing effective support to clinicians and staff. Maintain a calm and professional reception area, addressing disruptive behaviours politely and safely, and escalating to management when necessary.Stay informed of any updates or changes in practice guidance and team procedures. Assist in training new reception team members. Front Desk: Be the first point of contact for patients, projecting a positive and friendly image to patients and visitors. Assist with any queries, whether in person, over the phone, or online. Handle patient enquiries efficiently and courteously. Manage the flow of patients arriving at the reception for appointments or inquiries. Process payments and issue receipts for non-NHS services. Ensure the reception area, noticeboards, and leaflet dispensers are clean, tidy, and free from obstructions. Registrations and Appointments: Register new patients and schedule appointments. Assist with care navigation, helping patients find the most appropriate clinician or service, both within and outside the practice. (Training will be provided.) Monitor incoming E-Consult messages, scheduling appropriate appointments or directing them to appropriate member of staff. Accurately record and assess requests for emergency appointments / home visits based on urgency, following practice protocols. Once trained, act as a chaperone for patients during GP appointments when requested. Arrange interpreting services for patients as needed. Communication: Answer incoming phone calls promptly and professionally, ensuring calls are documented and acted upon or redirected as appropriate. Coordinate with GPs, Nurses, and the clinical team to relay information, follow up on documentation, results, and appointments. Monitor the reception email account, actioning requests and escalating urgent matters to them to appropriate member of staff when necessary. Liaise with GP's and clinicians to forward concerns, follow up on samples, letters, prescriptions, and other paperwork. Prescriptions and Certificates: Assist with processing prescriptions and addressing patient queries related to prescriptions. Handle Cremation Forms and Death Certificates, notifying relevant departments and accurately documenting details of the passing. Data Handling: Timely action EMIS tasks and DOCMAN workflow. Update and maintain patient records through accurate data entry. Manage incoming correspondence via post and electronically. Miscellaneous: Safely accept and record vaccine/medication deliveries, ensuring correct storage and informing relevant departments. Open and lock practice premises as needed, ensuring security protocols are followed. General Duties: Collaborate professionally with colleagues at Albany House Surgery, fostering strong working relationships. Contribute to the development of services, including improving processes, templates, and principles. Participate in any required statutory, mandatory, or additional training and development programs.
